page: Microsoft Azure FX32mds_v2 is a compute-focused and memory-dense virtual machine powered by Microsoft Hyper-V. The server features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates a deep cache hierarchy comprising 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced CPU features including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated encryption instructions like VAES and SHA-NI.

The hardware configuration provides 672.0 GB of system RAM, delivering an unusually high ratio of 21.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 1888 GB local NVMe SSD, providing low-latency temporary storage alongside Azure Premium Storage capability. The server operates without discrete GPU accelerators, relying solely on Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions for vector and matrix computations.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-thread capabilities, with Geekbench single-core reaching a top-tier score of 2313.0 and strong Geekbench multi-core performance of 18003.0. Memory throughput reflects the hardware density, yielding strong uncached large-block bandwidth with 232.79 GB/s read and 136.78 GB/s write speeds. Compression and decompression tests excel, achieving 34.68 GB/s in single-threaded gzip and 200.05 GB/s in multi-threaded bzip3. While smaller LLM inference tests (135M and 7B parameter models) demonstrate strong prompt processing throughput, CPU-bound generation on larger models such as a 70B parameter network drops to 2.72 tokens per second due to the absence of dedicated GPUs.

The qualitative profile represents high resource density per instance, combining high-frequency clock rates with extensive memory capacity and fast NVMe storage. It is best suited for compute-heavy relational and in-memory databases, memory-intensive electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, batch data compression, and mid-scale CPU-based machine learning inference.
